title: Incident owner, root cause, and fix spread across turns, with the wrong fix corrected at the end
notes: Root cause and an initial (WRONG) fix are stated several turns apart; the true fix is only revealed in a correction near the end, separated from the root cause by an unrelated noise turn. Tests that the extractor doesn't stop at the first-mentioned fix and does capture that it did not actually work.

turns.text: We've got a P2 incident: checkout latency spiked 3x starting around 09:00.
I'm taking IC for this one — assigning myself.
Quick unrelated note, the standup got moved to 15 minutes later today.
Back to the incident — root cause looks like connection-pool exhaustion on the payments DB.
Makes sense given the latency pattern.
Applied a fix: bumped the pool size from 10 to 40 connections.
That should help. Any confirmation yet?
Correction on the fix — bumping the pool size alone didn't work, latency was still elevated. What actually fixed it was killing a stuck long-running query that was holding connections open.
Got it — the pool-size bump wasn't the real fix; killing the stuck query was.

gold_atoms.text: A P2 incident (checkout latency 3x spike from around 09:00) was caused by connection-pool exhaustion on the payments DB, driven by a stuck long-running query holding connections open.
Killing the stuck long-running query resolved the incident — merely bumping the connection pool size from 10 to 40 did NOT fix it.

forbidden_items: Bumping the connection pool size to 40 fixed the incident
Increasing the pool size resolved the latency spike
